detail:
NIDDK describes management of chronic kidney disease as centered on protecting the kidneys from further damage and slowing progression. The institute identifies blood pressure control as the most important step in treating kidney disease, alongside blood glucose management for people with diabetes. Sources describe regular monitoring with the same blood and urine tests used in diagnosis, so the care team can track changes in kidney function and damage over time.

NIDDK notes that many people with CKD are prescribed medicines to lower blood pressure, control blood glucose, and lower cholesterol, and that two classes of blood pressure medicines, ACE inhibitors and ARBs, may slow kidney disease in some people. The sources also describe working with a registered dietitian on a kidney-aware meal plan, heart-healthy eating, physical activity, and caution with regular use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, which can damage the kidneys.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about managing chronic kidney disease.
sourceName: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
summary: NIDDK describes CKD management centered on blood pressure control, blood glucose management in diabetes, ongoing blood and urine monitoring, kidney-protecting medicine classes, and dietitian-supported meal planning.
takeaways: blood pressure control is described as the most important step in treatment
monitoring tracks kidney function and damage with blood and urine tests over time
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Chronic Kidney Disease: protecting kidneys and slowing progression
